events.description: First US counterterrorism drone strike, in Yemen, killed Abu Ali al-Harithi.
First reported Pakistan drone strike killed Pakistani Taliban leader Nek Muhammad.
Al-Qaeda transatlantic airliner plot against jets leaving Heathrow, orchestrated from Waziristan.
Bush administration ramped up Pakistan drone campaign to about 35 strikes.
Pakistan drone campaign peaked (about 117 strikes).
Failed Times Square bombing; Hakimullah Mehsud's group sent Bill Roggio a video claiming responsibility.
Mustafa Abu al-Yazid killed in a drone strike.
Bin Laden letter ordered operatives to relocate to Nuristan, Kunar, Ghazni and Zabul.
Bin Laden told Atiyah Abd al-Rahman to get the brothers out of Waziristan and into Afghanistan in small groups.
John Brennan claimed there had not been a single collateral death in covert drone strikes.
Osama bin Laden killed in a raid in Abbottabad.
Anwar al-Awlaki killed in a drone strike.
Obama speech selectively quoted bin Laden on airstrikes and reserves.
Nasir al-Wuhayshi killed in a US drone strike, with at least three senior lieutenants.
US raid killed Abu Khalil al-Sudani in Paktika; seized information led to a later raid on al-Qaeda camps in Shorabak, Kandahar.
Farouq al-Qahtani killed in a US air strike in Afghanistan, days before the US presidential election.
Last recorded drone strike in Pakistan.
AQAP leader (al-Wuhayshi's replacement, Qasim al-Raymi) killed.
Anwar al-Awlaki killed in a US drone strike in Yemen
Awlaki's 16-year-old son Abdulrahman killed in a drone strike. The hosts say it targeted AQAP's media emir.
Special forces raid in Yemen killed Awlaki's young daughter
Abu al-Khayr al-Masri killed by an R9X blade-equipped missile (a Hellfire variant) in Idlib
US strike killed Baitullah Mehsud's wife, uncle and some of his children. The hosts give no date.
US military released its tally of about 113 civilians killed in air strikes in Afghanistan, Somalia and Syria. Host said it came out 'yesterday'.
UK drone strike killed ISIS virtual plotter Reyaad Khan, the first targeted UK drone strike outside a conventional battle
US/AFRICOM conducted a peak of 55 strikes in Somalia. The AFRICOM commander said al-Shabaab controlled 25% of Somalia.
125 US strikes against AQAP in Yemen, about one every three days
Qasim al-Raymi escaped from prison in Yemen
Qasim al-Raymi, AQAP emir, killed in a strike in Yemen
After Wuhayshi's death AQAP took over Hadramawt province and its capital for almost a year

key_claims: About 95% of recorded Pakistan drone strikes hit North and South Waziristan, although al-Qaeda had a wide footprint in Karachi, Quetta, Islamabad, Peshawar and elsewhere.
Drone strike data exposed the 'wheel of jihad': al-Qaeda, the Haqqani Network, TTP, IMU and TIP operated together, refuting the 'disconnected dots' view.
The Haqqani Network is an integral part of the Afghan Taliban and both fought in Afghanistan and sheltered al-Qaeda in North Waziristan.
Mustafa Abu al-Yazid was al-Qaeda's leader and liaison to the Afghan Taliban in Afghanistan, showing the Taliban-al-Qaeda tie.
Atiyah Abd al-Rahman described al-Qaeda at 'medium tempo' at the height of the 2010 drone campaign, so drones were tactically useful but not strategically decisive.

After bin Laden's late-2010 orders, al-Qaeda moved leaders and families from Waziristan into Afghanistan (Nuristan, Kunar, Ghazni, Zabul), and figures like Farouq al-Qahtani and Abu Khalil al-Sudani were later killed there.
Obama's 2013 speech cherry-picked a bin Laden quote; bin Laden actually wanted reserves kept away from air-strike-prone fronts.
US drone strikes in Pakistan stopped being reported after 2018, partly because Pakistani press reporting was locked down.
Drone strikes suppress the threat and disrupt command and control. The hosts say their overall effect on al-Qaeda affiliates is hard to judge and that drones are a tactic, not a strategy.
Al-Qaeda affiliates are resilient. Qasim al-Raymi began jihad in the 1990s and led AQAP for five years, and Khalid Batarfi waited years to succeed him.
After Wuhayshi was killed, AQAP took Hadramawt and its capital for almost a year and then replaced him. Strikes hurt the group but did not stop its insurgency.
AQAP complains of Saudi, US and British spies placing tracking devices on cars and homes. The hosts think jihadist counterintelligence has since improved.
Abu al-Khayr al-Masri, a chief lieutenant of Zawahiri, was killed in Idlib in early 2017 by an R9X missile. The hosts cite it as evidence of US efforts to limit civilian casualties.
Somalia is now the main drone theater, with 55 AFRICOM strikes in 2019. Al-Shabaab still controls about 25% of Somalia despite the loss of senior leaders.
The hosts argue Awlaki's son and daughter were casualties of war, and that AQAP both eulogized the son as a 'lion of the jihad' and claimed he was a civilian.
Drone use is spreading: the UK killed Reyaad Khan in 2015, and ISIS and Jund al-Aqsa have adapted commercial drones for combat.
